title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
claim: Direct addition of carbonate salts can template lanthanide clusters but is generally discouraged at atmospheric pressure; slow in situ generation of carbonate, or CO2 fixation under controlled pH, is preferred so that carbonate precipitation does not outrun hydrolysis and cluster assembly.
explanation: Na2CO3 successfully templated Gd14 and Dy14 cores in which μ3-, μ4- and μ5-carbonate ions sit on triangular, quadrilateral and pentagonal faces. The authors nonetheless say added carbonate tends to precipitate lanthanide carbonate before cluster cores form. Supporting slow-release cases include capsule-like Ln24 clusters in which both dimethylcarbamate and μ4-CO3 arise from DMF at 160 °C, and La7, Ln12, Ln27 and Ln37 clusters in which carbonate is taken up from air.
scope: Carbonate-templated lanthanide clusters, especially giant cages and wheels.
conditions: Ln24 examples: isonicotinic acid, CuO and Ln(NO3)3·6H2O in DMF at 160 °C. Air-derived carbonate examples include methanol (La7), mixed EtOH–CH3CN (Ln37), and ligand systems that fix CO2 without added carbonate salts.
caveats: Direct carbonate addition is shown to work for the chiral Ln14 pair, so the warning is a practical tendency, not an absolute prohibition.
